sections.text: # Lakatos and Research Programs: Hard Core, Protective Belt, Progressive vs. Degenerating

metadata.title: Lakatos and Research Programs: Hard Core, Protective Belt, Progressive vs. Degenerating

sections.text: ## The Big Picture

metadata.title: Lakatos and Research Programs: Hard Core, Protective Belt, Progressive vs. Degenerating

sections.text: Imre Lakatos's Methodology of Scientific Research Programs (MSRP) is the most sophisticated attempt to preserve Popperian falsificationism while accommodating Kuhn's historical observations. Lakatos saw himself as Popper's defender against Kuhn — but in defending Popper he significantly transformed him. His central move: shift the unit of appraisal from the individual theory to the **research program** — a sequence of theories sharing a common core plus methodological strategies for protecting and extending it.

metadata.title: Lakatos and Research Programs: Hard Core, Protective Belt, Progressive vs. Degenerating

sections.text:
```
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|              RESEARCH PROGRAM STRUCTURE (MSRP)                   |
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                                                  |
|  HARD CORE                                                       |
|  +---------------------------------------------------------+     |
|  |  The unfalsifiable (by decision) center:                |     |
|  |  Core theoretical commitments protected by convention   |     |
|  |  Newton's laws of motion + universal gravitation        |     |
|  |  → "Do not blame Newton's laws if anomaly appears"      |     |
|  +---------------------------------------------------------+     |
|           |                                                      |
|           v  protected by                                        |
|  NEGATIVE HEURISTIC                                              |
|  "Do not direct modus tollens at the hard core"                  |
|           |                                                      |
|           v  directs attention toward                            |
|  PROTECTIVE BELT                                                  |
|  +---------------------------------------------------------+     |
|  |  Auxiliary hypotheses that absorb empirical failures:   |     |
|  |  - Initial conditions                                   |     |
|  |  - Background assumptions                               |     |
|  |  - Measurement theories                                 |     |
|  |  - Ancillary assumptions                                |     |
|  |  These can be revised when anomalies appear             |     |
|  +---------------------------------------------------------+     |
|           |                                                      |
|           v  directed by                                         |
|  POSITIVE HEURISTIC                                              |
|  "Investigate these anomalies, extend the program this way"     |
|  Research agenda: what to work on next                           |
|                                                                  |
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

sections.text: ## The Hard Core

metadata.title: Lakatos and Research Programs: Hard Core, Protective Belt, Progressive vs. Degenerating

sections.text: The hard core consists of the central theoretical commitments of the research program — the propositions that define the program's identity and that scientists within the program agree, by convention, not to revise.

metadata.title: Lakatos and Research Programs: Hard Core, Protective Belt, Progressive vs. Degenerating

sections.text: ### Newtonian Mechanics as the Paradigm Case

metadata.title: Lakatos and Research Programs: Hard Core, Protective Belt, Progressive vs. Degenerating

sections.text:
| Hard Core Component | Statement |
|--------------------|-----------|
| **N1** | Every body perseveres in a state of rest or uniform motion in a right line unless compelled to change its state by forces impressed thereon |
| **N2** | The change of motion is proportional to the motive force impressed (F = ma) |
| **N3** | To every action there is always opposed an equal reaction |
| **N4** | The force of gravity between two bodies is proportional to their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance |

metadata.title: Lakatos and Research Programs: Hard Core, Protective Belt, Progressive vs. Degenerating

sections.text:
These are the hard core of Newtonian mechanics as a research program. When a planet's orbit doesn't match predictions, Newtonian scientists do not question N1–N4. They look for:
- Unknown masses (another planet perturbing the orbit)
- Errors in initial conditions
- Missing forces (tidal effects, radiation pressure)

metadata.title: Lakatos and Research Programs: Hard Core, Protective Belt, Progressive vs. Degenerating
Lakatos and Research Programs: Hard Core, Protective Belt, Progressive vs. Degenerating

sections.text: ## The Negative Heuristic

metadata.title: Lakatos and Research Programs: Hard Core, Protective Belt, Progressive vs. Degenerating

sections.text: The negative heuristic is the methodological decision: **do not direct modus tollens against the hard core**. This is a convention — a research strategy, not a logical necessity. Scientists protecting the hard core from anomalies is not dogmatism; it is a reasonable methodological strategy that enables a program to be developed fully.

metadata.title: Lakatos and Research Programs: Hard Core, Protective Belt, Progressive vs. Degenerating

sections.text: Kuhn's observation that scientists protect their paradigm against anomalies is thus, on Lakatos's account, not irrational but rather the correct expression of the negative heuristic.

metadata.title: Lakatos and Research Programs: Hard Core, Protective Belt, Progressive vs. Degenerating

sections.text: ## The Positive Heuristic

metadata.title: Lakatos and Research Programs: Hard Core, Protective Belt, Progressive vs. Degenerating

sections.text: The positive heuristic specifies the research agenda: which mathematical techniques to develop, which model simplifications to relax, which anomalies to prioritize. It is the program's guide to self-development.

metadata.title: Lakatos and Research Programs: Hard Core, Protective Belt, Progressive vs. Degenerating

sections.text:
```
NEWTONIAN POSITIVE HEURISTIC (rough structure):
  1. Model planets as point masses (simplification)
  2. Add perturbations for multi-body interactions
  3. Add corrections for non-spherical bodies
  4. Add corrections for relativistic effects (small)
  5. If anomaly persists: search for undetected mass

metadata.title: Lakatos and Research Programs: Hard Core, Protective Belt, Progressive vs. Degenerating

sections.text:
The positive heuristic tells you where to invest research
effort BEFORE you know the results. A program with a rich
positive heuristic can absorb failures while maintaining
a productive research agenda.
```

sections.text: ## Progressive vs. Degenerating Research Programs

metadata.title: Lakatos and Research Programs: Hard Core, Protective Belt, Progressive vs. Degenerating

sections.text:
This is Lakatos's key normative distinction. A research program is **progressive** if:
1. Each successive theory in the sequence has **excess empirical content** over its predecessor — it predicts novel facts
2. Some of those novel predictions are **confirmed**

metadata.title: Lakatos and Research Programs: Hard Core, Protective Belt, Progressive vs. Degenerating

sections.text:
A research program is **degenerating** if:
1. Theory revisions only explain anomalies **after the fact** (ad hoc)
2. No novel predictions are generated or confirmed
3. The program is "always burying its failures"

metadata.title: Lakatos and Research Programs: Hard Core, Protective Belt, Progressive vs. Degenerating

sections.text:
```
+---------------------------+---------------------------+
|  PROGRESSIVE PROGRAM      |  DEGENERATING PROGRAM     |
+---------------------------+---------------------------+
|  T1 → T2 → T3 → T4       |  T1 → T2 → T3 → T4       |
|                           |                           |
|  Each Ti predicts novel   |  Each Ti adjusts to      |
|  facts not predicted by   |  explain anomalies that  |
|  Ti-1                     |  Ti-1 couldn't handle    |
|                           |                           |
|  Some predictions         |  No new predictions      |
|  confirmed                |  confirmed               |
|                           |                           |
|  Program growing          |  Program shrinking        |
|  theoretically and        |  to its core;            |
|  empirically              |  belt thickening         |
+---------------------------+---------------------------+
```

sections.text: ### Neptune: The Progressive Belt Modification

metadata.title: Lakatos and Research Programs: Hard Core, Protective Belt, Progressive vs. Degenerating

sections.text: The best case for Lakatos's framework:

metadata.title: Lakatos and Research Programs: Hard Core, Protective Belt, Progressive vs. Degenerating

sections.text:
```
TIMELINE:
  1846: Uranus orbit deviates from Newtonian predictions

metadata.title: Lakatos and Research Programs: Hard Core, Protective Belt, Progressive vs. Degenerating

sections.text:
OPTIONS:
  (a) Reject Newton's laws (Popperian naive response)
  (b) Assume undetected mass (belt modification)

metadata.title: Lakatos and Research Programs: Hard Core, Protective Belt, Progressive vs. Degenerating

sections.text:
Le Verrier and Adams: option (b)
  Calculate where the disturbing planet must be

metadata.title: Lakatos and Research Programs: Hard Core, Protective Belt, Progressive vs. Degenerating

sections.text:
Result: Astronomers point telescope at predicted location
  Discover Neptune within 1° of prediction

metadata.title: Lakatos and Research Programs: Hard Core, Protective Belt, Progressive vs. Degenerating

sections.text:
→ PROGRESSIVE: novel prediction confirmed
  → Belt modification vindicated
  → Newtonian program gains credibility
```

sections.text: ### Prout's Hypothesis: The Degenerating Program

metadata.title: Lakatos and Research Programs: Hard Core, Protective Belt, Progressive vs. Degenerating

sections.text: William Prout (1815): all atomic weights are integer multiples of hydrogen's weight. When anomalies appeared (chlorine ~35.5), the theory was adjusted: "errors in measurement," "mixtures of isotopes," etc.

metadata.title: Lakatos and Research Programs: Hard Core, Protective Belt, Progressive vs. Degenerating

sections.text: Each adjustment was ad hoc — explaining the anomaly but predicting nothing new. The program degenerated. Prout's hypothesis was eventually abandoned, but only when atomic theory provided a better framework that explained why some elements have non-integer average atomic weights (isotopic mixtures).

metadata.title: Lakatos and Research Programs: Hard Core, Protective Belt, Progressive vs. Degenerating

sections.text: ### Bohr's Atomic Model: Degenerating That Became Progressive

metadata.title: Lakatos and Research Programs: Hard Core, Protective Belt, Progressive vs. Degenerating

sections.text: The Bohr model (1913) initially looked degenerating — it was inconsistent with classical electrodynamics and required ad hoc quantization rules. Lakatos's point: you should not abandon a program prematurely. After years of anomalies and adjustments, the quantization rules became the foundation for wave mechanics (Heisenberg/Schrödinger 1925–26) — a genuinely progressive development.

sections.text: ## The Timing Problem

metadata.title: Lakatos and Research Programs: Hard Core, Protective Belt, Progressive vs. Degenerating

sections.text: When exactly should a scientist abandon a degenerating program? This is Lakatos's most serious gap. His criteria are **retrospective**: we can identify a program as degenerating or progressive after the fact, but we cannot always tell in real time.

metadata.title: Lakatos and Research Programs: Hard Core, Protective Belt, Progressive vs. Degenerating

sections.text:
```
LAKATOS'S ADMISSION:
  "We can call a series of theories... progressive only
   in retrospect... one may never know when a programme
   has 'degenerated' irreversibly... we may never know
   whether a programme is progressing or degenerating."

metadata.title: Lakatos and Research Programs: Hard Core, Protective Belt, Progressive vs. Degenerating

sections.text:
IMPLICATION:
  Scientists cannot use MSRP as a decision procedure.
  It is a rational reconstruction of science's history,
  not a methodology that guides individual decisions.

metadata.title: Lakatos and Research Programs: Hard Core, Protective Belt, Progressive vs. Degenerating

sections.text:
FEYERABEND'S ATTACK: If MSRP cannot guide real-time
decisions, it is not a methodology — it is a
rationalization written after the fact.
```

sections.text: ## Feyerabend's Critique: "Anything Goes"

metadata.title: Lakatos and Research Programs: Hard Core, Protective Belt, Progressive vs. Degenerating

sections.text: Paul Feyerabend was Lakatos's colleague at the LSE and his friendly adversary. Their intended joint book, one defending a methodology and one attacking it, was never completed — Lakatos died in 1974.

metadata.title: Lakatos and Research Programs: Hard Core, Protective Belt, Progressive vs. Degenerating

sections.text:
Feyerabend's argument in *Against Method* (1975):
1. Any proposed methodological rule — including Lakatos's — has been violated by the most successful episodes in science
2. Galileo, Copernicus, Newton violated the "best" methodologies of their day
3. Restricting science to any methodology would have slowed progress
4. Conclusion: "The only principle that does not inhibit progress is: **anything goes**"

metadata.title: Lakatos and Research Programs: Hard Core, Protective Belt, Progressive vs. Degenerating

sections.text: Feyerabend is deliberately provocative. "Anything goes" is not a positive principle but the absence of normative constraints — an **epistemological anarchism**. His point is that the history of science undermines every proposed methodological norm.

metadata.title: Lakatos and Research Programs: Hard Core, Protective Belt, Progressive vs. Degenerating
